pyautogui.press('esc')

pyautogui.doubleClick(x=275, y=291, duration=0.2)

# Click the blank Slide 2 thumbnail (second rectangle below Slide 1) in the Slides pane to make Slide 2 active
pyautogui.click(x=100, y=345, duration=0.3)

# Click the second thumbnail (blank white rectangle labeled “2”) in the Slides pane to activate Slide 2
pyautogui.click(x=92, y=268, duration=0.3)

# Click near the center of the blank Slide 2 thumbnail in the left pane to make Slide 2 active
pyautogui.click(x=125, y=279, duration=0.3)

pyautogui.press('pagedown')

# Double-click near the center of the blank Slide 2 canvas to create/activate a text box for entering text
pyautogui.doubleClick(x=700, y=350, duration=0.3)

# Press F2 to activate the text box tool so we can place a text box and type "Page 1" on the blank Slide 2
pyautogui.press('f2')

# Click on the center area of the blank Slide 2 canvas to create the text box for entering "Page 1"
pyautogui.click(x=682, y=350, duration=0.2)

# Type "Page 1" into the active text box on Slide 2
pyautogui.typewrite("Page 1")
